findings.title: MCP tool outputs are unbounded - no truncation or size caps on any of the 6 tool results
findings.description: buff_expand embeds the FULL generated Rust source in the tool text (tools.rs:638-642); buff_check returns every diagnostic uncapped (399-428); buff_complete serializes the entire CompletionResponse (510-525); buff_format returns full source (596-600). Grep for truncat/max/cap/limit in buff-mcp/src returns zero matches. Large .buff inputs funnel megabytes into agent context windows. Verified: no outbound LLM calls, no API keys, stdio-only, tools-only capabilities (no sampling).
findings.root_cause: T62 shipped a thin delegation layer (every handler returns ToolResult::ok(text) verbatim) with no output-budget policy; cost hygiene was out of the task spec.
findings.impact: AI agents consuming buff-mcp can burn unbounded context tokens per tools/call on big files or error-heavy projects; repeated buff_check loops on a large project multiply cost. No repo-side API bill (server is local), so severity stays low.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared output budget in ToolResult (e.g. 64 KiB): over-cap results get head+tail slices, byte counts, and an elision note pointing at the equivalent CLI command for full output.
findings.fix_guide: 1. Add MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT const + elide() helper in tools.rs (or ToolResult::ok). 2. Route all six handle_* success paths through it. 3. Append an explicit [truncated: N of M bytes] note (agents reason better with explicit elision). 4. Unit test with a >64KiB fixture asserting the elision marker appears. 5. Note the budget in crates/buff-mcp/AGENTS.md MCP TOOLS table.

effort_estimate.breakdown: helper+const 15m; rewire 6 handlers 15m; unit test 15m; AGENTS.md note 15m

detection_method.query: (?i)(truncat|max_?bytes|MAX_OUTPUT|char_limit|cap_) over crates/buff-mcp/src -> 0 hits; manual read of tools.rs handlers

confidence.rationale: Full read of all six handlers confirms zero truncation logic; only uncertainty is whether a cap lives in buff-lsp handlers (delegated outputs return verbatim LSP shapes).

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Direct code reading shows ToolResult::ok/to_json pass text through unmodified; no cap exists anywhere in the crate. Severity deliberately low because cost lands on the agent user's local context window, not a hidden API spend.

findings.title: buff ai context generates an unbounded context pack and instructs pasting the entire file into an AI tool
findings.description: build_context_pack walks every .buff file under project_root (collect_buff_files:572-604 skips target/node_modules/.git/hidden but has no depth, file-count, or size cap), enumerates ALL PreludeType/AssocFn/InstanceFn signatures, then prints or writes the pack; header says 'Paste this entire file into your AI tool'. On a large repo the paste target grows without bound. Command is otherwise CLEAN: fully offline (doc: 'does NOT call any AI APIs'), no network, no shell-out, no API keys; verify path is local T55 typecheck + Levenshtein hints.
findings.root_cause: T65 optimized for grounding quality (enumerate everything) with no output budget; cap-free collect_buff_files and unbounded String growth by design.
findings.impact: Users pasting into metered AI tools (Copilot/Claude) can ingest hundreds of KiB of prelude signatures per session. User-side cost only; no hidden spend. Deliberate trade-off, hence low severity.
findings.recommendation: Emit a stderr size warning above a threshold (e.g. 256 KiB) and add --max-bytes or --symbols-only mode so users can slim the pack before pasting; keep default behavior unchanged.
findings.fix_guide: 1. Add MAX_PACK_BYTES const + stderr note in run() Context arm. 2. Optional: AiCmd::Context gains --max-bytes; when exceeded, drop section 4 (Per-Type Method Signatures, the largest) first. 3. Update pack header text. 4. Extend context pack test with a size-threshold unit test.

detection_method.query: build_context_pack + collect_buff_files audit for caps; grep (?i)(truncat|max|limit|budget) in commands/ai.rs -> 0 hits

confidence.rationale: Full 797-line read: no network, no Command, no API keys anywhere; unbounded pack confirmed by code shape. Score below 1.0 because 'unbounded' depends on user project size, a judgment call.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Offline behavior is explicit in the module doc and confirmed by zero network primitives; the finding targets only the missing size guard, which grep proves absent. Severity low since the paste is user-initiated.
